verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents several first-party headless paths: a Terraform/OpenTofu provider for infrastructure as code, a CKS API to create, list, update and delete clusters, and an Inference API with generated clients. All of these authenticate with bearer API access tokens, and kubeconfig files let kubectl drive clusters without the Cloud Console. missing for 10: explicit CI pipeline guidance (e.g., CI runner examples or non-human service-account tokens), an official CLI, and independent or hands-on corroboration of automated use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The CoreWeave Terraform provider lets you manage CoreWeave infrastructure as code, including CKS clusters, VPC networking, AI Object Storage policies and buckets, and Managed Inference resources.
The API lets you create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters on CoreWeave infrastructure.
All API requests must include a CoreWeave API access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.
Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.
The CoreWeave Inference API provides programmatic control over inference gateways, model deployments, and capacity claims.
